registry_info.name: grain_block
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `grain` family's (a) dialect - solid|split|quartered|lattice|shell, carried by cube_scene, prism_block and grabbable_line. One 1 m block cut five ways at once, so the five words can be read across instead of chosen between.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. The five words, their ORDER and the family's own gauge are PRELOADED from cube_scene.gd at runtime (FAM.GRAINS, FAM.UNIT, FAM.SPLIT_GAP, FAM.QUARTER_GAP, FAM.LATTICE_GAP, FAM.SHELL_SECTION) and checked in both directions at _ready; do not retype them here or in the script. The two axes declared below are NOT that word - see dna.axis_shape for why it is exhibited rather than swept.

grain_block.name: Grain Block
grain_block.description: Five bays in a row, each holding the same 1 m block divided a different way: undivided, parted once through the horizontal mid-plane, quartered 2x2x2, latticed 3x3x3, and emptied to the twelve edges. The cell counts are cube_scene's own and the word list is read live out of its GRAINS const. `kerf` decides where the cut's own width is taken from - painted on the surface and taken from nothing (drawn), taken out of the pieces so the 1 m envelope holds (inward), put in between them so the block grows out of its unit (outward), or not taken at all, at which point four of the five bays are one photograph (shut). `reckoning` fills a register above each bay - one cell per piece (count), or a stacked bar whose ceiling is one whole block of material (mass) - or draws what the division removed back into the block itself, translucent and exactly complementary (void). Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random, and there is not one glyph anywhere on it.
interactions: set kerf=shut and watch four of the five words collapse into one cube
walk the row at kerf=inward and find the rung where the block stops being a divided solid and starts being a structure
set reckoning=mass and read the five bars: 1.000, 0.890, 0.705, 0.475, 0.124
set reckoning=count and notice the shell has fewer pieces than the lattice and a fifth of its material
set kerf=outward and see that nothing was removed at all - the seam was paid for with room, not with matter
grain_block.qfep_connection: The family's word says a solid can be divided more or less finely, and the arithmetic says that is not what its five values do. Two of them nest, one does not, and the last is a different operation carrying the same name - so the ladder is a category held together by a word rather than by an order. What `kerf` then exposes is that the difference between the values is not a property of the division at all: at kerf=shut the four cut bays are the same photograph, and every one of them becomes visible only because a constant nobody in this family states has been spent on opening the seams. The vocabulary is legible because of a decision it does not admit to making, and the decision has a cost that has to come out of either the material or the room.
grain_block.relationships: synthesis over the `grain` family's (a) dialect (cube_scene, prism_block, grabbable_line); refuses the (b), (c) and (d) dialects on the record in dna.declines; adopts its word by exhibiting rather than sweeping it, as taxonomy_hall does with `taxonomy` and instruction_bench with `tell`; reads both the word list and the gauge live out of cube_scene.gd

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The row is 7.80 m across five bays on a 1.70 m pitch and 1.22 m deep at its widest value, so an 8 x 2 clear strip with room to stand in front of it. Every bay reads from +Z and the row runs along X with the solid end at -X; `orientation: face_approach` plus a rotation in the map token is how you get that. There is no collider anywhere in the file, so the pathfinder routes straight through the blocks - which is correct, because there are no blocks, there are five pictures of one.
spatial_needs.shelf_rule: a space, not an object (base 7.80 m, h 2.12 m, registry.measurements)

measurements.measured_by: computed from the script's own layout constants and re-derived in a Python replica of the same geometry, rasterised at the sweep camera with a z-buffer; no Godot was run, per the brief. MeshInstance3D only, which is what the capture AABB counts, and every drawn node in this artifact is a MeshInstance3D holding a BoxMesh. X: five bays at 1.70 pitch run -3.40..+3.40, and the two end bays (solid, shell) are 1 m wide at every value, so the box is -3.90..+3.90 = 7.80 m and is fixed by two bays the kerf axis cannot touch. Y from 0 (every bay's underside, so the grid's base-to-floor grounding is a no-op and no auto_ground opt-out is needed) to 2.12, the top of the reckoning register: REG_Y 1.32 plus 7 x 0.08 + 6 x 0.04 = 0.80. The scribes at kerf=drawn stand 2 mm proud of five faces and NOT the underside, which is why the floor is exactly 0 at every value rather than -0.002 at one of them. Z -0.61..+0.61 is the lattice at kerf=outward, 1 + 2 x 0.11; at every other value the deepest thing is 1.00 m. The register never moves with kerf, so the only thing that changes the box at all is the two middle bays growing at `outward`, and neither of them reaches the ends.

dna.axis_shape:
THE EXHIBITED WORD IS MIXED, WHICH IS WHY IT IS EXHIBITED AND NOT SWEPT, and the case was read out of the members' CODE rather than their prose.

solid -> split NESTS: one cut plane at y = 0. split -> quartered NESTS: cube_scene's _build_quartered cuts at x = y = z = 0 and {y=0} is a subset of that, so the two halves ARE unions of the eight. quartered -> lattice DOES NOT NEST: _build_lattice puts twenty-seven 0.30 cubes on a 0.32 pitch, so its cut planes fall at +-0.16, and {0} is not a subset of {-0.16, +0.16} - no sub-cube of the eight is a union of sub-cubes of the twenty-seven. The rungs get finer without nesting. lattice -> shell IS NOT A CUT AT ALL: _build_shell adds no sub-cubes, it builds twelve struts of a different shape, and grabbable_line's _grain_part_count() returns 0 for shell, the one rung that draws no body, because for a segment the boundary IS the two endpoints.

Two rungs nest, one does not, and the last changes the operation from subtraction to structure. A mixed set cannot be swept without demolishing the comparison it exists to make, so all five stand at once and the axes vary two things the family never varies.

`kerf` SITS SIDE BY SIDE. Its four values are four answers to one question - where does the cut's own width come from - and no one of them contains another: `shut` takes nothing and shows nothing, `drawn` takes nothing and shows everything, `inward` takes it out of the material, `outward` takes it out of the room. shut and drawn are not a smaller inward; they remove no material at all.

`reckoning` SITS SIDE BY SIDE with a zero. `none` is the bare row; `count`, `mass` and `void` are three different quantities that do not contain one another and that RANK THE FIVE WORDS DIFFERENTLY - which is the finding the axis exists for. Both are named because they call for opposite handling under trimming: dropping the tail of a nested axis lowers a ceiling, dropping the tail of a parallel one loses a case.
dna.default:
kerf=inward, reckoning=none. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of PLACED artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom was spent on the strongest single reading.

WHY `inward` AND NOT `shut` OR `outward`. `shut` is the loudest value and the worst default: with the cells touching, solid, split, quartered and lattice are four photographs of one cube, and a visitor meeting the bench there meets a row that appears to say the vocabulary is empty. That collapse is the axis's sharpest finding and it is worth a tile, not the tile you arrive at. `outward` is the largest picture and the least like the family: nothing is removed, the blocks break out of their own unit, and the two middle bays crowd their neighbours - it is the alternative the family has never built, which makes it an argument rather than a baseline. `inward` is the discipline all three members actually hold: the seam is paid for out of the material and the 1 m envelope is preserved. It is the only value at which the five bays are five visibly different bodies, and measured in the replica it is also the value with the lowest subject share (9.44% against 13.01% at outward+mass), i.e. the least crowded frame.

WHY `none`. The reckonings are commentary on the row and the row has to be read first. A default carrying a register would make a visitor's first reading of the bench a reading of an instrument.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched. This is the cross-member argument the three (a) declarations leave unbuilt: each member stands ONE grain at a time, in one body, so no member can put `quartered` next to `lattice` and show that they do not nest, and no member can show that at zero seam four of its five words are the same picture. cube_scene has 155 placements and prism_block and grabbable_line 16; between them they have never once photographed two grains together.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT, AND WHAT THE ARITHMETIC SAID BACK.

(1) THE FAMILY'S OWN ENVELOPE CLAIM IS BROKEN BY MOST OF ITS OWN RUNGS. All three members say in prose that the silhouette is held constant and only the mass inside it changes. Measured off their code: cube_scene's split (two 0.48 slabs at +-0.26), quartered (eight 0.48 cubes at +-0.26) and shell (0.05 struts at +-0.475) land their outer faces on +-0.500 exactly; its lattice spans 0.94, 6.0% short, and cube_scene says so in its own comment. prism_block's quartered apex reaches 0.49667 (sub_scale 0.48, centroid 0.16667, push 0.010, lift 0.08), 0.67% short - and its SPLIT OVERSHOOTS: the upper piece is a PrismMesh of size (0.5, 0.5, 1.0) whose base is floated to y = 0.02, so its apex stands at 0.52, 4% PROUD of the unit it is supposed to fit. grabbable_line centres each part in its own pitch cell, so the outermost end is inset by 0.14 x pitch and the drawn extent is L(1 - 0.28/n): 86.0% at split, 93.0% at quartered, 97.7% at lattice - under a comment that says "the outermost pieces still reach the endpoints". Six deviations, in three directions, under one claim. `kerf=inward` is that claim stated exactly, and `kerf=outward` is the case they were all approximating away from.

(2) `lattice` IS NOT "MORE GAP THAN MATERIAL", AND THIS BENCH'S BRIEF SAID IT WAS. At cube_scene's own numbers the 3x3x3 holds 27 x 0.30^3 = 0.729 of the unit - 72.9% MATERIAL, 27.1% gap. Held to a strict envelope at the family's widest gap (0.04) it would be (1 - 2 x 0.04)^3 = 0.8847. It only crosses one half at a kerf of 0.10315 m, which is five times anything in the family and 6% below the 0.11 this bench needs to photograph the seam at all. So at this bench's gauge it IS more gap than material - 47.46% - and that is a fact about the gauge, not about the word. THE FIRST VALUE THAT IS GENUINELY MOSTLY VOID IS `shell`, at 12.39%, and shell is exactly the value that has stopped being a cut. The ladder does not become mostly void until the operation changes.

(3) THE TWO READINGS RANK THE FIVE WORDS DIFFERENTLY, WHICH IS WHY BOTH ARE IN THE REGISTER. Material still standing, at kerf=inward: 1.000, 0.890, 0.705, 0.475, 0.124 - monotone. Pieces: 1, 2, 8, 27, 12 - NOT monotone. The shell has fewer than half the pieces of the lattice and a quarter of its material. Whether shell is "finer" than lattice depends entirely on which quantity you read, and `reckoning` puts the two readings in the same rectangle above the same bay so the disagreement is one glance rather than an argument.

(4) THE MASS BAR ONLY MOVES AT ONE VALUE OF `kerf`, AND THAT IS THE POINT. At shut, drawn and outward nothing has been removed from any cut bay: all four read 1.000 and only the shell reads 0.124. At inward they read 1.000 / 0.890 / 0.705 / 0.475 / 0.124. Three of the four ways of showing a division take no material at all, so the bar is flat in three tiles out of four - not a dead instrument, a measurement of how rarely a drawn division is a real one.

(5) THE KERF IS ONE NUMBER READ FOUR WAYS, and it is the family's own number wherever the family's number is legible. _resolve_gauge() takes maxf(0.11, max(FAM.SPLIT_GAP, FAM.QUARTER_GAP, FAM.LATTICE_GAP)); today that is maxf(0.11, 0.04) = 0.11 and the bench widens, and if cube_scene ever opens past 0.11 the bench follows it rather than overruling it. The same number is then painted by `drawn`, subtracted by `inward`, inserted by `outward`, and set to zero by `shut`. The shell's strut section is maxf(0.11, FAM.SHELL_SECTION) on the same floor.

(6) COUNT THE THING YOU CLAIM TO COUNT. _build_cells and _build_shell RETURN the number of meshes they put in the tree, and _build_count is handed that number. The register cannot disagree with the block, and the shell is exactly twelve boxes because it is built as cube_scene builds it - twelve full-length struts overlapping at the corners, not twelve struts plus eight corner cubes, which would have been a nineteen-percent lie told by a redundant node.
dna.kin:
THE WORD IS TAKEN WHOLE AND NOT RETYPED. grain_block.gd opens with
const FAM := preload("res://commons/primitives/cubes/cube_scene.gd")
and the bays, their number and their ORDER come from FAM.GRAINS at build time, read as FAM.GRAINS rather than through Object.get() (a const is not a property, so get() returns null and the bench would fall back silently to a private copy) and rather than through get_script_constant_map() (non-static, cannot be called on the class at all). FAM.GRAINS also fails at PARSE time if the const disappears, which is a better failure mode than either. _check_family_words() runs at _ready and push_errors in BOTH directions: a word the family declares that this bench has no bay for, and a bay this bench builds that the family has dropped. FAM.UNIT, FAM.SPLIT_GAP, FAM.QUARTER_GAP, FAM.LATTICE_GAP and FAM.SHELL_SECTION are read the same way and are load-bearing, not decorative - see dna.note (5).

WHAT IS TRANSCRIBED, ON THE RECORD: the cells per axis. cube_scene does not expose them as constants - they are implicit in _build_split (one mid-plane), _build_quartered (a two-element sign array) and _build_lattice (range(-1, 2)) - so _cells() writes (1,2,1), (2,2,2) and (3,3,3) with that citation. It is the only geometry in this file that is copied rather than read, and the value LIST it is keyed by is not.

FOUR VOCABULARIES WEAR THIS ONE WORD, and the bench must say which it took:
  (a) solid | split | quartered | lattice | shell   cube_scene, prism_block, grabbable_line
      HOW A SOLID IS DIVIDED - the direction and scale at which a body gives way.
  (b) points | beads | stroke | flood               pedagogical_sketchbook
      HOW A MARK IS LAID DOWN - the sketchbook's grain is about the drawing hand.
  (c) rows | columns | diagonal | rings             rotate_grid_cubes
      THE ORDER A GRID IS READ IN - a traversal, not a division; nothing is cut.
  (d) meridian | parallel | even                    sphere_low
      HOW A SPHERE IS TESSELLATED - where a fixed budget of quads is spent.
This bench takes (a), which is the majority (3 of 6 declarations) and the only one of the four that is about the GRAIN OF A MATERIAL, which is what the word means outside this corpus: the direction and scale at which a solid gives way. (b) is mark-making, (c) is traversal order and (d) is tessellation. Three different words wearing this one, and naming them here is the point of the entry.

THE THREE MEMBERS OF (a) DECLARE THE SAME FIVE VALUES IN THE SAME ORDER, character for character, so there is no reordering question of the kind the `tell` family has. What differs is what the words land on: on a cube 1/2/8/27 pieces plus a 12-strut cage, on a triangular prism 1/2/4/9 plus a 9-strut cage (the triangle's own subdivision, half of it upside down), on a segment 1/2/4/12 plus two endpoint beads. This bench stands the CUBE, because the cube is the body all three compare themselves against and because the block is what the word is about.

THE PALETTE IS THE FAMILY'S, member by member. Block: grabbable_line.gd's line_color Color(0.788, 0.463, 0.996), taken as a plain StandardMaterial3D albedo because that is exactly what it is there - the one place in this family whose look is not a shader. Scribes: cube_scene.tscn's Grid.gdshader emissionColor Color(0.981557, 0.761247, 0.912913). Register ceiling: balance_puzzle.gd's platform_color Color(0.3, 0.3, 0.35). Ghosts: transform_puzzle_base.gd's ghost_color Color(0.0, 0.8, 1.0) at ghost_alpha 0.25, unshaded.

ONE SUBSTITUTION, AND IT IS NOT A DRIFT. cube_scene's own look is Grid.gdshader - a magenta wireframe with show_interior true. It is not used here, for two reasons stated together. First, a wireframe shader draws lines on every face, and this bench's whole subject is where the lines in a block come from; a shader that draws them for free would answer the question before it is asked. Second, headless Godot never reimports, so a shader edit does not reach the sweep and a stale compiled shader photographs as a dead axis - gyroid_demo read 0.00% on both of its axes across sixteen byte-identical tiles for exactly that reason. A bench whose subject is a comparison cannot afford a grain it cannot trust to be the same grain in every tile.
dna.declines:
`grain` IS REFUSED AS THIS ARTIFACT'S VARYING AXIS, on the record, and the refusal is the design. The case is MIXED (see dna.axis_shape): two rungs nest, one does not, and the fifth is a different operation. Sweeping it would photograph one rung per tile, which is exactly what the three members already do 171 times over, and the thing that cannot be photographed that way is the only thing this bench is for.

`along` IS REFUSED, AND IT IS THE INTERESTING DECLINE, because it is the half of the dictionary definition this bench does not deliver. Grain outside this corpus means the DIRECTION and the scale at which a solid gives way, and every member divides ISOTROPICALLY - cube_scene treats x, y and z alike at quartered and lattice, and its split is on y for no stated reason. An axis that moved the divisions onto one axis instead of three is the obvious second question, and it is arithmetically impossible on this ladder at a legible kerf. Holding the PIECE COUNT and spending it in one direction, `quartered` becomes eight beds: 8 cells and 7 kerfs in 1 m, so 7 x 0.11 = 0.77 m of kerf leaves 0.23 m for eight cells, 0.0288 m each, 1.7 px at this framing. `lattice` becomes twenty-seven beds, 26 x 0.11 = 2.86 m of kerf inside a 1 m block, which is not a thin axis but an impossible one. Holding the CUT COUNT instead, `split` and `quartered` both become a single cut on one axis and render as the same object - a designed 0.00% pair. Either way the axis is dead before it is built, and the arithmetic is written here so the next agent does not rediscover it.

`seam` IS REFUSED AS A NAME for the kerf axis, and it was a near thing. escher_staircase and florensky_sphere already declare seam: none | hairline | gap | scaffold | field, and the first three rhyme with this bench exactly. But there the question is WHERE THE IMPOSSIBILITY IS PUT - `none` means the discontinuity has been smoothed away so there is no seam at all, which is a fact about the FIGURE, where this bench's zero is a fact about the DRAWING (the cut is still there, it is just shut). And `scaffold` and `field` name a rigged interval and an even distribution of blame that a divided block has no analogue for. Taking a word without its answers is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary, so the word is declined and `kerf` used instead - the carpenter's word for the width a cut takes out, unused across all 470 declared axis names, and in the same register as `grain`.

`account` IS REFUSED for the second axis for the same reason: the four translation cubes declare account: ghost | sweep | terminus | formula | none, which asks how a MOTION is accounted for. `none` and `ghost` would fit; `sweep`, `terminus` and `formula` name a path, an endpoint and an equation, none of which a static block has. `reckoning` is unused. So are `kerf`, `void` and `mass` as axis names; `count` is unused as an axis name and `unit` is used once, for a polyhedron family, with no overlap.

`stock` IS REFUSED. pick_up_cube declares stock: wire | foam | crate | steel | clay - what a cube is MADE of - and `wire` is very nearly this bench's `shell`. But the rest of that list is a material palette, and a bench that changed the material of five blocks would be measuring shaders, which is the one thing dna.kin says this artifact must not do.

THE TOP-FACE SCRIBES ARE NOT WIDENED, deliberately. At kerf=drawn a band normal to Z reads 2.79 px on the top face against 5.21 px on the +X face, because the camera pitches only 14.9 degrees down and the top is heavily foreshortened. Widening the top bands alone would make the kerf TWO numbers and break the one thing this axis is - a single width read four ways - so the number is recorded here instead. Every cut is legible on at least one visible face at 5.21 px or better; none is legible on all three.

TIME IS REFUSED. The strongest unbuilt axis on this family is the ORDER the cuts are made in, and whether a block that has been quartered can still be latticed. Every value of it is a fact about a sequence and the evidence here is ONE STILL PNG per value; info_board was swept across five duration exports and produced six identical tiles. Declined rather than shipped as a finished-looking experiment.

TEXT IS REFUSED. There is not one Label3D and not one glyph in this file. A bay is identified by what it draws, which is the whole point of the word, and a caption would let a reader agree with the bench without looking at it. LabelFramer therefore has nothing to hang panels behind and nothing enters or leaves the capture AABB on that account.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency and not in changed pixels, because a prediction in the wrong units is a prediction about a different instrument. artifact_dna_critic.py crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralises each frame's own corner background, converts to greyscale, RESIZES TO 160 x 160 and takes the mean of the hottest 5% (1,280 samples). Every number below comes from rebuilding this exact geometry in Python and rasterising it at this exact camera (RES 760, FOV 34, YAW 0.62, PITCH -0.26, PAD 1.9, dna.framing 0.60) with a z-buffer, the sweep's own key (1.25, rot -42/-35/0) and fill (0.45, rot -20/130/0), its ambient Color(0.62,0.65,0.72) at 0.55, its background Color(0.055,0.055,0.070) and its FILMIC tonemap, then pushing the result through that same pipeline.

READ EVERY NUMBER AS A FLOOR. A flat rasteriser has no shadows, no ambient occlusion and no antialiasing, and every prediction in this corpus that named a pair and a number has under-predicted, by 1.5x to 6.7x. BUT NOTE WHERE THAT RULE BREAKS: those four predictions were 0.11% to 4.18%, with the whole scale above them. The numbers here are 13% to 65%, and a 6.7x multiplier is not available at the top of a metric that saturates at 100. The floor rule still applies - a sweep BELOW these numbers means something is broken - but do not expect the multiplier.

THE CLOSEST PAIR ON THE WHOLE SHEET IS `kerf` shut <-> inward AT reckoning=void, PREDICTED 13.16%. THE ARITHMETIC, and it is a claim about interference rather than about size: at `shut` the cells touch and the block is a full 1 m body; at `inward` the same block has 0.11 m slots taken out of it, which is normally the loudest thing the kerf axis does (16.95% at reckoning=none). At reckoning=void those slots are FILLED with the translucent complement, so the block reads as a full 1 m body again and the only difference left is that the filling is cyan at 25% alpha instead of purple at 100%. The ghost of what was removed hides the removal. If this pair comes back near 25% the ghosts are not drawing; if it comes back near 5% the block is not.

CLOSEST BY VALUE PAIR ON `kerf`: drawn <-> shut, predicted mean 16.38% (floor 14.58% at reckoning=mass, ceiling 17.31%). Those two values build the SAME BODY - twelve or twenty-seven touching cells filling exactly 1 m - and differ only by the scribes, which are 0.11 m bands on five faces: 10 bands at quartered and 20 at lattice, 2 at split, 0 at solid and 0 at shell. Second closest: inward <-> shut at 16.88%, i.e. the two are predicted to be A DEAD HEAT 0.50 POINTS APART, which is itself a falsifiable claim. If the sweep separates them by more than about three points, one of the two is drawing something the replica does not model.

CLOSEST BY VALUE PAIR ON `reckoning`: none <-> count, predicted mean 34.88% (floor 33.32% at kerf=outward). The count register is 50 small cells above five bays; against an empty register that is the smallest of the six reckoning pairs because a 0.08 m cell is 5.4 px and the register is only 30 x 63 px of a 573 x 279 px subject.

AXIS MEANS PREDICTED, over the 24 same-axis pairs each: `kerf` frame 2.97% / focus 40.31% -> BITES. `reckoning` frame 3.39% / focus 51.07% -> BITES. Widest pair on the sheet: `kerf` inward <-> outward at reckoning=void, 65.27%. THESE ARE LOUD NUMBERS AND THEY ARE MEANT TO BE READ AS SUCH: both axes change bodies rather than details, on a bright subject against a near-black ground, so any silhouette shift of more than a few pixels saturates the hottest 5%. A verdict of `bites` on this sheet is worth very little; the two structural claims below are what this pass is actually staking.

CLAIM ONE, AN EQUALITY: `kerf` CANNOT TOUCH TWO OF THE FIVE BAYS. `solid` has no cut for a kerf to be taken from, and `shell` is not made by cutting - _build_shell never reads the kerf, because a boundary is not a cut. Rendered ALONE at the same camera, those two bays must be IDENTICAL TO THE BYTE across all four kerf values. Measured in the replica: solid 0/255, shell 0/255, against 234, 239 and 239 for split, quartered and lattice. FALSIFIER: any non-zero difference in an isolated render of either bay. In the FULL frame they are not quite constant, and the reason is stated rather than discovered - the bays overlap in screen x (113 px of separation against a 114 px silhouette), so at `outward` the quartered and lattice blocks grow into their neighbours' crops.

CLAIM TWO, A SECOND EQUALITY ACROSS SIX MEASUREMENTS: EVERY `reckoning` PAIR MUST READ THE SAME AT kerf=shut AS AT kerf=drawn. Those two values build identical blocks and differ only by surface scribes, which are common to both frames of any reckoning pair and therefore cancel out of the difference; no reckoning is drawn where a scribe is. Predicted spreads, all six pairs: 0.0000 points (none<->count 35.399 both, none<->mass 64.115 both, none<->void 39.772 both, count<->mass 51.418 both, count<->void 55.706 both, mass<->void 64.328 both). FALSIFYING THRESHOLD: 0.5 points on any pair. A percentage can be right by luck; six exact equalities cannot.

AND ONE PAIR PREDICTED **NOT** TO BE DEGENERATE, because it looks as though it should be. `reckoning` mass <-> count fill the SAME rectangle above the same bay and are the obvious twin candidate on a 16-tile sheet. Predicted 50.38% (47.25-51.42): not a twin, eight times the critic's 6% twin bar. A solid bar and a grid of 27 cells at 60% coverage disagree over most of the register, and the register is where the hottest pixels of that pair all are.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL SIXTEEN VARIANTS, not from the default. Union 7.80 x 2.12 x 1.22 (x = the two end bays, which no axis moves; y = the bays' underside at 0 to the top of the reckoning register at 1.32 + 0.80; z = the lattice at kerf=outward, 1 + 2 x 0.11), diagonal sqrt(60.84 + 4.4944 + 1.4884) = sqrt(66.8228) = 8.17452, radius 4.08726. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 would put the camera at 4.08726 / 0.3057307 x 1.9 = 25.4013 m and show a 15.532 m frame around a 7.80 m object.

AT 0.60 the camera comes to 15.2408 m and the frame to 9.3190 m, which is 81.554 px per metre. Rasterised at that setting and measured across all sixteen tiles, the subject's bounding box runs x 127..700 and y 265..544 - margins of 127 px left, 60 right, 265 top, 216 bottom - and the subject covers 9.44% of the frame at its emptiest tile (inward, none) and 13.01% at its fullest (outward, mass).

THAT IS A SPARSE SUBJECT, NOT A SMALL ONE, and the distinction is taxonomy_hall's. The bounding box spans 75.4% of frame width by construction; five separated blocks with an empty register above them are mostly air, so a pixel count against the background reads low for a correctly framed object. The critic's own blank-render bar is BLANK_SUBJECT = 0.002 and floating_sphere_field is a legitimate artifact at 0.83%. Do not tighten this framing on subject share alone. The tall top and bottom margins are the fit-by-DIAGONAL cost on a wide flat subject: a 7.80 m row inside a bounding sphere sized by its own diagonal leaves the vertical thirds empty, and buying them back costs the right margin, which is the near end of an obliquely-viewed row and therefore the magnified one.

TWO OTHER VALUES WERE MEASURED AND REJECTED. 0.58 gives 84.3 px/m and 9.8% subject - better on both - but leaves 47 px of margin on the RIGHT; taxonomy_hall rejected 43 px there for the showcase key light's specular fringe, which the replica does not model, and 47 px is not enough more. 0.61 gives 68 px of right margin at 80.2 px/m, and at that gauge the worst slot falls to 5.13 px. 0.60 is the value where the tight margin is 60 px and nothing that carries meaning has fallen under 5 px.

GAUGE CHECK AT 81.554 px/m, BECAUSE THE FAMILY'S OWN NUMBERS DO NOT SURVIVE A FIVE-UP FRAME. From this standpoint a world displacement projects to screen at 0.8275 of its length along X, 0.9664 along Y and 0.6176 along Z, and a slot's legibility is the PERPENDICULAR width of its band on whichever face it opens onto. Measured, at kerf 0.11: a slot normal to X reads 7.30 px on the +Z face and 3.73 px on the top; normal to Y, 8.16 px on +X and 8.53 px on +Z; normal to Z, 5.21 px on +X and 2.79 px on the top. So 5.21 px is the binding case and 0.11 m is the smallest hundredth of a metre that clears five. cube_scene's own gaps are 0.04, 0.04 and 0.02, which land at 1.89, 1.89 and 0.95 px here - they are sized for a capture of ONE cube filling the frame, exactly as instruction_bench found of the `tell` family's marks. The re-gauge is a WIDENING and _resolve_gauge takes maxf(0.11, the family's widest), so it can only ever widen.

EVERYTHING ELSE, CHECKED: lattice cell 0.26 m -> 17.5 px. Shell strut 0.11 m -> 7.4 px. Register cell 0.08 m -> 5.4 px, register 0.44 x 0.80 m -> 30 x 63 px. A 1 m block's screen silhouette is 1.395 m -> 114 px, against a bay separation of 1.70 x 0.8139 = 1.384 m -> 113 px, so adjacent bays just touch at inward and overlap at outward. Nothing that carries meaning is under 5 px except the top-face scribes at 2.79 px, which are recorded in dna.declines and deliberately not widened.

THE ROW RUNS ALONG X AND NOT IN A 2 x 3, and that was a decision. A block grid fills a square frame better and would have raised px/m by about a quarter, but the camera pitches only 14.9 degrees down and a block is 1 m tall: a front block would black out the bottom two thirds of the one behind it. A row costs frame area and loses nothing to occlusion. It was also NOT rotated to face the standpoint, which would have bought 23% more separation per metre of row (P instead of P cos 0.62) and would have been an artifact built around one camera - the exact fault probe_anamorphic.py exists to catch.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED IS NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body, no signal connection, no collider and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children and its own ancestors' metadata. _ready is ungated: it reads config metadata, checks the family's word list in both directions, resolves the gauge, makes four materials and builds the whole bench standalone, so the sweep's rescue path (call apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire.

THE FAMILY IS READ, NEVER RUN. FAM is a preloaded SCRIPT and only its constants are touched - FAM.GRAINS, FAM.UNIT, FAM.SPLIT_GAP, FAM.QUARTER_GAP, FAM.LATTICE_GAP, FAM.SHELL_SECTION. CubeScene is never instantiated, so its _ready never runs, no cube is built and nothing is added to the tree from that side.

THREE WAYS IN, ONE DOOR. The sweep sets the @export properties directly before add_child; the grid stamps config_kerf / config_reckoning metadata, which _read_grid_config_meta walks up to four ancestors for before _ready builds; and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary. All three are validated against KERFS and RECKONINGS, and apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY when a value actually changed AND _ready has already built once - the force_pad fault. An unrecognised word keeps the standing value rather than emptying the bench.

BOTH AXES ARE String ENUMS, not bools, so the fixture-string trap (a typed bool rejecting the string "true" before _ready) cannot occur. Neither axis uses the word "true" or "false" for any value, so nothing can arrive from a JSON spec as a boolean.

DETERMINISM: every dimension in the file is a constant or a product of constants and _spans(). Two boots produce the same box list on any machine, and two captures of one value are two photographs of one object.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a flat number is read correctly.

THE SOLID BAY AND THE SHELL BAY ARE CONSTANT ACROSS `kerf`, BY CONSTRUCTION AND ON PURPOSE. solid has n = 1 on every axis, so _spans returns the same single interval at every mode; shell never calls _spans at all. A future reader who crops to either bay and reports `kerf` INERT will have measured the argument and called it a bug: those two bays ARE the argument, because they are the two values of the exhibited word that are not made by cutting. Rendered alone they are 0/255 apart across all four kerf values.

THE `void` REGISTER IS EMPTY IN FOUR BAYS AT TWO VALUES OF `kerf`. At shut and at drawn nothing has been removed from solid, split, quartered or lattice - the cells touch and fill the envelope exactly - so the only ghost in those tiles is the shell's hollow. This is a CONDITIONAL pair, not a twin: the critic's own conditional check groups by VALUE PAIR across contexts, and none<->void should be read that way (predicted 39.77% at shut and drawn, 41.59% at inward, 40.76% at outward - flatter than it sounds, because the shell's ghost alone already saturates the hottest 5%).

THE MASS BAR IS IDENTICAL AT shut, drawn AND outward. Nothing is removed at any of them, so four bays read a full bar and only the shell is short. It moves at `inward` alone. That is finding (4) in dna.note and it is a measurement, not a dead instrument.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `kerf`: the solid bay, the shell bay, and the register's position and capacity. CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `reckoning`: every block in every bay - the reckonings add and never subtract.

NO TEXT ANYWHERE. Not one Label3D, not one glyph, in any tile.

THE CAPTURE AABB IS THE REAL BODY. Every drawn node is a MeshInstance3D holding a BoxMesh. There is no MultiMeshInstance3D, no CSG, no particle system and no Label3D, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present. The two end bays fix the X extent and no axis moves them, so the union pre-pass fixes the camera and only the middle bays growing at `outward` touch the box at all.

THE Z-STACK, because a frame is four rails and not a slab. The register occupies y 1.32..2.12 and the tallest block is 1.22, so there is 0.10 m of clear air under it and it stands in front of nothing. The ghosts at reckoning=void are the exact COMPLEMENT of the material and are therefore disjoint from it - no ghost is ever in front of a piece it comments on; they occupy precisely the space the pieces do not. The scribes at kerf=drawn stand 2 mm proud of the faces they mark and cover nothing but those faces. WITHIN a block, the near cells occlude the far ones and the seams are the apertures; at inward+lattice the centre cell is entirely hidden, which is the reading, not a fault. BETWEEN bays, screen separation is 113 px against a 114 px silhouette, so adjacent bays touch at shut / drawn / inward and overlap at outward, where a nearer bay (larger x) covers the far edge of the one behind it.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, CHECK THREE THINGS BEFORE THE DESIGN.
(1) Was --max at least 16? At the gallery's default cap of 9 a 4x4 declaration renders 4x2 and `reckoning` is measured on {none, mass} alone - a verdict about two values published as a verdict about four. The axis is declared none / mass / void / count precisely so that a capped run drops `count` first, which is the closest pair; it costs the piece-count finding, which is stated here.
(2) Was the sweep run --staged? A 7.80 m row is over the 6 m staging cut-off so no plinth should be added, but if one is, the pair AABB grows and every slot shrinks below its 5 px gauge.
(3) Is the standpoint doing the work? The five bays rank in screen X and the canonical camera sees the row at 35.5 degrees off its axis. A probe from directly above would separate the lattice's slots far more strongly and would flatten the register into its own footprint; one from along the row would stack the bays into each other. Per the standing gate an INERT verdict on this token is not reportable until tools/probe_anamorphic.py has been run on it.
